md: - **Rajamannar Committee (1969):** set up by the **Tamil Nadu** (DMK) government under **Dr P.V. Rajamannar** to study Centre-State relations; report **1971**; asked for the **immediate setting up of the Inter-State Council** under **Article 263**. The **Sarkaria Commission** also recommended a permanent ISC, which was set up in **1990**.
- **UGC motto:** **"Gyan-Vigyan Vimuktaye"** (Knowledge Liberates), shown in Devanagari in the UGC logo.

- **Vijay Kelkar Committee (2015):** revisiting and revitalising the **PPP model** of infrastructure; report to the Finance Minister **November 2015**.
- **Uday Kotak Committee (2017):** set up by **SEBI** on **corporate governance** of listed companies; report **October 2017**.
- **Sanjay Agrawal Committee (July 2022):** former Agriculture Secretary; on **MSP**, **natural farming** and **crop diversification**.

- **Garbhini-GA2**: **first India-specific AI model** to estimate the **age of a foetus** in the **second and third trimesters**; built under **GARBH-INi** (DBT) by **IIT Madras** and **THSTI, Faridabad** (February 2024); uses Indian population data instead of Western formulae.

- **PM Vishwakarma** (**17 September 2023**, **Ministry of MSME**): for artisans in **18 traditional trades**; **collateral-free loan up to ₹3 lakh** in two tranches (**₹1 lakh + ₹2 lakh**) at **5%** interest; **toolkit incentive up to ₹15,000** (e-voucher); stipend **₹500 a day** during training.

- **Law Commission Report No. 279** (**22nd Law Commission, 2023**) - "Usage of the Law of Sedition": recommended **retaining Section 124A IPC** with the **Kedar Nath Singh (1962)** safeguards and higher punishment.

- **[4 Nov 2026] RBI Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets (TCCFM)**: chaired by the **RBI Deputy Governor in charge of the Financial Markets Regulation Department**; **7 external members** (SBI, Axis, ICICI, Citibank, Morgan Stanley, CCIL, ex-SEBI member); covers **money, government securities, forex and derivatives** markets; meets **at least once a quarter**.

- **New ₹20 banknotes (17 May 2025):** **RBI** announced ₹20 notes in the **Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series** bearing the signature of Governor **Sanjay Malhotra**; design unchanged; all old ₹20 notes **remain legal tender**.

- **Largest trading partner 2024-25:** the **USA** for the **fourth year in a row** – two-way trade **$131.84 billion** (exports $86.51 billion). **China** second ($127.7 billion), with India's trade deficit with China at a record **$99.2 billion**.

- **Intra-industry trade:** a country **exports and imports goods of the same industry at the same time** (e.g. cars both exported and imported). **Inter-industry trade** = exchange of goods of different industries. Measured by the **Grubel-Lloyd index**.

- **New funds in Budget 2025-26:** **Urban Challenge Fund of ₹1 lakh crore** – cities as growth hubs, funds up to 25% of the cost of bankable projects (₹10,000 crore for 2025-26); a **Makhana Board in Bihar** for production, processing and marketing of makhana.

- **International Development Association (IDA):** World Bank Group arm set up in **1960**; gives **zero- or low-interest loans ("credits") and grants** to the **poorest countries** – the World Bank's concessional (soft-loan) window.
- **Later use:** The **Chola** bronzes of South India, such as the **Nataraja**, were also cast by the **lost-wax** method.

- **Order of Oman (First Class):** conferred on **PM Modi** by **Sultan Haitham bin Tarik** in **Muscat** on **18 December 2025**; the order was instituted in **1970** by Sultan Qaboos bin Said. India and Oman also signed a **free trade agreement** during the visit.

- **Yuva and Bal Sahitya Puraskar 2025 (Telugu):** announced **18 June 2025**. **Yuva Puraskar** (writers under 35) – **Prasad Suri**; **Bal Sahitya Puraskar** – **Gangisetti Sivakumar** for the story "**Kaburla Devatha**".

- **National Sports Awards 2025** (announced **18 August 2026**): **no Khel Ratna** for 2025 – the first such year since **2014**; **17 Arjuna** awardees, incl. **Divya Deshmukh** (chess), **Tejaswin Shankar** (athletics), **Gayatri Gopichand** (badminton); selection panel headed by former SC judge **Arun Kumar Mishra**.
- **Khel Ratna 2024** (given January 2025): **Manu Bhaker**, **D. Gukesh**, **Harmanpreet Singh**, **Praveen Kumar**.

- **India Open 2026 (Super 750, New Delhi, January 2026):** men's singles – **Lin Chun-yi** (Chinese Taipei) beat **Jonatan Christie** 21–10, 21–18; women's singles – **An Se-young** (South Korea) retained her title, beating **Wang Zhiyi** (China) 21–13, 21–11.
- **Lakshya Sen – Australian Open Super 500 2025:** won the men's singles title in **Sydney** on **23 November 2025**, beating Japan's **Yushi Tanaka** 21–15, 21–11 – his first title of 2025.

- **BHISHM cubes to the Maldives (July 2025):** During PM Modi's state visit, India handed over **two Aarogya Maitri Health Cubes** at **Male** on **25 July 2025**; run by the Maldives Emergency Medical Service. **BHISHM** = **Bharat Health Initiative for Sahyog, Hita and Maitri**.
- **BHISHM cubes to Kyrgyzstan (28 April 2026):** Defence Minister **Rajnath Singh** handed over **two sets of BHISHM Cubes** (Project Aarogya Maitri) to Kyrgyzstan in **Bishkek**.
- **Kyrgyzstan – national symbol:** President **Sadyr Japarov** signed a decree on **30 December 2023** recognising the **snow leopard** as the **national symbol** of Kyrgyzstan.
- **Papua New Guinea:** PM **James Marape** became the **first Pacific leader to address Australia's Parliament** (**8 February 2024**).
- **Mitra Shakti:** India–**Sri Lanka** Army exercise, held alternately in the two countries; **11th edition** at the Foreign Training Node, **Belagavi, Karnataka** (10–23 November 2025).
- **AFINDEX:** **Africa–India Field Training Exercise** of the Indian Army; 1st edition **2019, Pune**; 2nd edition **AFINDEX-2023** with **23 African nations** at **Aundh, Pune** (March 2023).
- **INS Sarvekshak:** hydrographic survey ship – **first Indian Navy ship to install a solar power system** (Green Initiative, February 2017); **18 flexible panels of 300 W** each.
- **UNCCD COP17:** **17–28 August 2026**, **Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia**; theme **"Restoring Land, Restoring Hope"**.
- **CMS COP15:** 15th COP of the **Convention on Migratory Species**, **23–29 March 2026**, **Campo Grande, Brazil**.
- **Glyptotermes chiraharitae** (APPSC PYQ): a dampwood **termite** from **Malabar WLS (Kakkayam), Kozhikode, Kerala**; described in **2016**; name from Sanskrit *chiraharita* = **evergreen**.

- **Cyclone names (North Indian Ocean):** given by **RSMC New Delhi (IMD)** from a list of **169 names** – 13 each from the **13 WMO/ESCAP Panel** countries – released in **April 2020**; a used name is not repeated.
- **Forbes World's Billionaires List 2026** (40th, released **10 March 2026**): richest person **Elon Musk** (about **USD 839 bn**), top for the second year; a record **3,428** billionaires.

# Records and UN Advocacy Roles

- **January Tali** (Arunachal Pradesh) – **first Indian woman** to summit both **Mount Kun (7,077 m)** and **Mount Nun (7,135 m)** in the **same season** (27 July – 8 September 2026).

- **NIMAS, Dirang** (National Institute of Mountaineering and Adventure Sports) – team led by **Col Ranveer Singh Jamwal** made the first ascents of **20 unclimbed peaks above 6,000 m** in the **Ladakh Range** in **23 days**; flagged in by Defence Minister **Rajnath Singh** on **25 September 2026**.

- **Smriti Mandhana** (cricketer) – named **UNICEF India Celebrity Advocate** on **11 October 2026** (**International Day of the Girl Child**); focus on **adolescent girls**.
- **NBPW sites:** found mostly in the **Ganga valley** – **Hastinapur, Kaushambi, Shravasti, Ayodhya, Varanasi, Rajgir, Pataliputra, Vaishali, Champa**; also **Ujjain, Vidisha** and **Taxila**.

- **Kondapur (Sangareddy district, Telangana):** a fortified **Satavahana** town; finds include **terracotta figurines**, **beads** and many **Satavahana coins**. Its site museum is run by the **ASI**.
- **Name:** The name **Vishnukundi** is generally taken as the Sanskrit form of **Vinukonda**, a hill-fort town in the Guntur (now **Palnadu**) region.

- **Territorial units:** The kingdom was divided into **Rashtras** and **Vishayas** (e.g. **Palki Rashtra, Karma Rashtra, Guddadi Vishaya**).
- **Army:** Fourfold – elephants, chariots, cavalry, infantry; **Hastikosa** = in charge of elephant forces, **Virakosa** = in charge of land forces.

- **2024 Lok Sabha election:** held in **seven phases** from **19 April to 1 June 2024**; votes counted on **4 June 2024**. Andhra Pradesh voted for the Lok Sabha and its Assembly in phase 4 on **13 May 2024**.

- **EWS quota:** **103rd Amendment Act, 2019** gave **10%** reservation to Economically Weaker Sections; upheld by a five-judge Bench by **3:2** in **Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India** (**7 November 2022**).

- **e-RUPI:** launched by **PM Narendra Modi** on **2 August 2021**; developed by **NPCI** on the UPI platform with the **Department of Financial Services**, **MoHFW** and the **National Health Authority**; a cashless, purpose-specific **e-voucher** (QR code or SMS string).

- **World Disasters Report:** annual report of the **International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC)** on disasters, deaths, people affected and losses; the 2022 edition was titled "Trust, Equity and Local Action".

- **Millennium Development Goals (MDGs):** **8 goals** from the **UN Millennium Declaration (September 2000)**, with **2015** as the target year; Goal 1 – eradicate extreme poverty and hunger; replaced by the **SDGs** from **2016**.

- **Census 2011 – most populous States:** **Uttar Pradesh (1st, ~19.98 crore, 16.5%)**, Maharashtra (2nd), Bihar (3rd), West Bengal (4th), **undivided Andhra Pradesh (5th, ~8.46 crore)**; Madhya Pradesh 6th.

- **Earliest metal:** **Copper** was the **first metal** used in India, in the **Chalcolithic** (copper-stone) age; the name comes from Greek *khalkos* (copper) + *lithos* (stone), as copper and stone tools were used together. Iron came later.
- **Lauriya Nandangarh** (West Champaran, Bihar): pillar with a **single lion** capital; bears **Pillar Edicts I–VI** in Brahmi.

- **Earliest copper-plate grant (Andhra):** the **Patagandigudem** copper plates of Ikshvaku king **Ehuvala Chamtamula** (3rd c. CE) are the earliest known copper-plate land grant of south India; they record a grant to a **Buddhist monastery**.

- **Somadeva Suri** (Jain, 10th c.; not Somadeva of Kashmir): wrote the Sanskrit champu **Yashastilaka** (c. 959 CE) at **Gangadhara** in the **Vemulavada Chalukya** kingdom, and **Nitivakyamrita** on statecraft.

- **Motupalli:** also called **Desiyakkonda-pattanam**; the Kakatiya king **Ganapatideva** set up a pillar edict (**Abhaya Sasana**, 1244-45 CE) here, assuring safety to sea traders whose ships were wrecked on his coast and fixing only the usual customs duties.

- **Trinidad and Tobago oil spill (February 2024):** a capsized barge (**Gulfstream**) leaked heavy fuel oil off **Tobago's** south-west coast; PM **Keith Rowley** declared a **national emergency** (11 February 2024).

- **INTERPOL notices:** **Red** – arrest or provisional arrest of a wanted person with a view to **extradition**; **Yellow** – locate a **missing person**; **Blue** – collect more information on a person's identity, location or activities; **Black** – information on **unidentified bodies**.

- **Colombo Process:** regional consultative process of **Asian countries of origin** of migrant workers (overseas employment and contractual labour); **12** member states; secretariat hosted by **IOM, Geneva**; non-binding, decisions by consensus; **India chairs it for 2024–26** – the first time.

- **Windsor Framework (27 February 2023):** UK–EU deal (**Rishi Sunak** and **Ursula von der Leyen**) amending the **Northern Ireland Protocol** of the Brexit Withdrawal Agreement; eases checks on goods from Great Britain to **Northern Ireland**; adds a **'Stormont brake'** on new EU rules.

- **Chicago Convention (7 December 1944):** Convention on **International Civil Aviation**, signed by 52 countries at Chicago; created the **ICAO** (in being from **1947**), headquartered at **Montreal**.
- **Greenpeace:** began in **1971** with a protest voyage from **Vancouver** against US nuclear tests; **Greenpeace International** (1979) is based in **Amsterdam**.

- **Deepavali** inscribed on UNESCO's **Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity** on **10 December 2025**, at the **20th session** of the Intergovernmental Committee held at the **Red Fort, New Delhi** (8–13 Dec 2025) – the first such session hosted by India.

- **UNESCO Creative Cities Network:** **Lucknow** named a **City of Gastronomy** (31 October 2025, World Cities Day) – India's second after **Hyderabad**; **Kozhikode** became India's first **City of Literature** and **Gwalior** a **City of Music** (2023).

- **Exploration Museum, Húsavík (Iceland):** covers the **Apollo astronauts' geology training in Iceland (1965 and 1967)**, Viking exploration and Arctic explorers; its **Astronaut Monument** (2015) names the **32** Apollo astronauts trained there.
- **France** – first country to explicitly guarantee the freedom to have an **abortion** in its **constitution**: joint session of Parliament at **Versailles**, **4 March 2024** (**780–72** votes).
- **Remittances (World Bank estimate, 2024):** **India** the **largest recipient** – about **USD 129 billion**; then **Mexico (USD 68 bn)** and **China (USD 48 bn)**.
- **Great Reset:** **World Economic Forum** initiative launched in **June 2020** by **Klaus Schwab** with the then **Prince of Wales (Charles)**, for a sustainable recovery after COVID-19.
- **Logistics Performance Index 2023 (World Bank):** **India 38th of 139** countries – up six places from **44th (2018)**.

- **Paris 2024 – India's 6 medals (1 silver, 5 bronze):** **Neeraj Chopra** – silver, men's **javelin**; **Manu Bhaker** – bronze, women's **10 m air pistol**, and bronze, **10 m air pistol mixed team** with **Sarabjot Singh**; **Swapnil Kusale** – bronze, men's **50 m rifle 3 positions**; **Aman Sehrawat** – bronze, men's **57 kg freestyle** wrestling; **men's hockey team** – bronze.
- **38th National Games (2025):** hosted by **Uttarakhand**, **28 January – 14 February 2025**; **Services (SSCB)** topped with **68 gold (121 medals)**; **Maharashtra** second, **Haryana** third.
- **Frankfurt Book Fair 2026 (78th):** **7–11 October 2026**; Guest of Honour **Czechia**; 75 Czech authors attended.

- **UN International Years 2026:** **International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists** (FAO; A/RES/76/253), **International Year of the Woman Farmer** (FAO; A/RES/78/279), **International Year of Volunteers for Sustainable Development** (A/RES/78/127).
- **Surajmal (Bharatpur):** Jat ruler of Bharatpur (ruled 1755-1763). A contemporary historian called him "the Plato of the Jat tribe" for his political wisdom.
- **Domingo Paes:** **Portuguese** traveller (horse trader from Goa); visited **Vijayanagara** c. **1520** in **Krishnadeva Raya's** reign; said the city seemed **as large as Rome**.
- **Unit sizes:** a **sar-i-khail** commanded **10 horsemen**; a sipah-salar commanded 10 sar-i-khails, and so on up to the khan (decimal system).
- **War elephants:** keeping elephants was a **privilege of the Sultan** alone; a **separate department** trained and maintained them.

- **Bhairavakona:** in the **Nallamala hills (Prakasam district)**; **eight rock-cut cave temples of Shiva**, cut in one rock face, c. **7th–8th century CE**; Shiva is worshipped here as **Kala Bhairava**.
- **Sapta Godavari:** the sacred tank (**pushkarini**) of the **Bhimeswara temple, Draksharama**; legend says the **Sapta Rishis** brought its water, which is used for the god's **abhisheka**.

- **Army modernisation:** Mir Qasim built a new army trained on **European lines**; the Armenian **Gurgin Khan** organised its artillery and musketeers, and a **gun factory (arsenal)** was set up at **Monghyr**.
- **Kotappakonda:** Hill near **Narasaraopet** in **Palnadu district**; its temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** as **Trikoteswara Swamy**; famous for its **Maha Shivaratri** festival.

- **Panchacharyas:** Veerashaiva tradition names five founding acharyas - **Revanaradhya (Renukacharya)**, **Marularadhya**, **Ekoramaradhya**, **Panditaradhya** and **Vishwaradhya**; their five peethas are at Rambhapuri (Balehonnur), Ujjaini, Kedar, Srisailam and Kashi.

- **Alberuni's book:** **Kitab-ul-Hind** (also called **Tahqiq-i-Hind**), completed about **1030 CE**, describes Indian religion, philosophy and science; translated into English by **E.C. Sachau** as *Alberuni's India*.

- **Kshetrayya:** Telugu composer of **padams** (sringara songs), linked with **Movva (Muvva)**, Krishna district; signature (mudra) **Muvva Gopala**. Patron: **Vijayaraghava Nayaka**, the **last Nayaka king of Tanjore**.
- **Kridabhiramamu:** Telugu play by **Vinukonda Vallabharaya** that describes life in **Orugallu (Warangal)**; English edition *A Lover's Guide to Warangal*.
- **Ismail Adil Shah (Bijapur):** lost the **Battle of Raichur (1520)** to **Krishnadevaraya** of Vijayanagara, who then took the **Raichur fort**.
- **Doji Bara (Skull) famine:** **1791–92**; hit **Madras** and the nearby regions after the monsoon failed for several years from 1789.

- **Chanda Railway agitation (1883):** protest in **Hyderabad State** against extending the **Nizam's State Railway** to **Chanda** with a guaranteed return to a London company; **Dr Aghorenath Chattopadhyaya** (Principal, Hyderabad College) called a public meeting and was removed from the State.
- **Bombay Municipal Act, 1872:** drafted and backed by citizens led by **Pherozeshah Mehta**; set up a Corporation in which **half the members were elected** by ratepayers.
- **Calcutta Corporation Act, 1899 (Curzon):** **reduced the elected members** and increased nominated ones; **28 members resigned** in protest.

- **Akbar's Goa mission (Jesuits):** at Akbar's request the **first Jesuit mission from Goa** reached his court in **1580**, led by Father **Rudolf Acquaviva** with Father **Antonio Monserrate** and Brother Francis Henriques. They brought a printed **Polyglot Bible**; Akbar had its Christian pictures shown to his painters.

- **Siddhacharyas – Charyapada:** the **Charyapada** (Charyagiti) are mystic songs of the Buddhist **Siddhacharyas** (Luipa, Kahnapa and others, 9th-11th c.) – the **earliest Bangla poems**. **Haraprasad Shastri** found the palm-leaf manuscript in the **royal court library of Nepal (1907)**.
- **Padma Shri:** **Shaik Nazar** (Guntur) received the **Padma Shri in 1986** for the folk art of **Burrakatha**.
- **Mohammedan Literary Society:** founded at **Calcutta in 1863** by **Nawab Abdul Latif** (its secretary) to spread **Western education** and modern ideas among Muslims.
- **Nandalal Bose:** led the team of Santiniketan artists that **illustrated the original handwritten Constitution of India**; the calligraphy was by **Prem Behari Narain Raizada**.
- **Raja Ravi Varma** (Kilimanoor, Travancore): set up the **Ravi Varma Fine Art Lithographic Press** at **Bombay in 1894**, which spread his prints of gods and epics across India.

- **Malkapuram inscription** (Guntur district, Sanskrit in Telugu script): of **Rudramadevi's** time; records the gift of **Mandadam (Mandara)** village to Ganapatideva's guru **Visvesvara Sambhu**, who set up a Saiva matha, a Sanskrit college, a **maternity home (Prasuti Sala)** and a free **hospital (Arogya Sala)** there.

- **Kondapalli fort – architecture:** on a **granite hill**; main gate **Dargah Darwaza** (named after the tomb of **Gulab Shah**, killed in battle there); **Golconda Darwaza** at the other end, towards Jaggayyapeta; palace **Tanisha Mahal** between two hills. Came under the **Sultan of Golconda in 1531**.

- **Classical language status:** **Telugu** and **Kannada** were declared classical on **31 October 2008** (Ministry of Culture). Criterion (2005): **high antiquity of early texts/recorded history over 1500–2000 years**. Total classical languages now **11** (Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, Bengali added on **3 October 2024**).
- **On women:** "I measure the progress of a community by the degree of progress which women have achieved." – **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**.
- **Ram Rajya:** Gandhi defined **Ramarajya** as the **sovereignty of the people based on pure moral authority** (Harijan, 1937); he said it did **not mean Hindu Raj**.
- **Khadi tour (April 1929):** Gandhi toured Andhra for **khadi**; he visited **Bezawada** and laid the foundation stone of the **Saraswata Niketanam** library building at **Vetapalem**.

- **Savarkar:** **V.D. Savarkar** was elected **president** of the Hindu Mahasabha in **1937** (**Ahmedabad** session) and held the post till **1943**; in his Ahmedabad address he said Hindus and Muslims were "two nations in the main".

- **Party newspapers:** **Justice** (English daily, from 26 Feb 1917) – edited by **Dr T.M. Nair**; **Dravidan** (Tamil, 1917); the party also took over the Telugu paper **Andhra Prakasika** (A.C. Parthasarathi Naidu).

- **Andhra Sahitya Parishat today:** moved from Madras to **Kakinada** (1919-20); since **1973** it is the **Andhra Sahitya Parishat Government Museum and Research Institute, Kakinada**, under the AP Department of Archaeology and Museums – palm-leaf manuscripts, copper plates, coins, sculptures.
- **RTE in force:** **Article 21A** and the **RTE Act, 2009** came into effect on **1 April 2010**.

- **Kundurti Anjaneyulu (1922-1982):** called **"Vachana Kavitha Pitamaha"** (father of free verse in Telugu); founded the **Free Verse Front**; **Sahitya Akademi Award 1977** for ***Kundurti Kritulu***.
- **Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao:** wrote the novel ***Chaduvu*** (1952); editor of the children's magazine ***Chandamama*** from 1952 till his death in 1980.
- **Potti Sriramulu's fast (1952):** began on **19 Oct 1952** at **Bulusu Sambamurthy's house in Mylapore, Madras** – the only Congress leader who gave him shelter; Sriramulu died on **15 Dec 1952**.

- **Jammu and Kashmir:** under the **Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order, 1954**, **Part IV (DPSP)** did not apply to J&K. The Presidential order **C.O. 272 of 5 August 2019** superseded the 1954 Order and applied **all provisions** of the Constitution to J&K.

- **Article 370 judgment (11 Dec 2023):** a **five-judge** Constitution Bench headed by CJI **D.Y. Chandrachud** upheld the abrogation **unanimously**; it directed J&K Assembly elections by **30 September 2024** and restoration of statehood at the earliest.
